newsitem.title: USA: HHS will act soon on U.S. home heating aid request.
newsitem.headline: HHS will act soon on U.S. home heating aid request.

text.p: The Clinton administration said Friday it would respond quickly to calls from a number of members of Congress that it release emergency funds to help low-income people pay their heating bills.
Forty-eight senators signed a letter to President Clinton urging him to immediately release $300 million in emergency Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) funds.

"An emergency condition currently exists because of skyrocketing energy costs and colder than normal temperatures in a large portion of the country," the letter, the most recent of several that have circulated in the House and Senate, said.

"We urge you to act quickly so that states can make the most efficient use of the funds and can assist families in the traditionally colder months of January and February," said the letter signed by senators of both parties.

"The letters are being carefully considered right now, and I'm sure the administration will respond quickly," said a spokesman for the Health and Human Services Department, which administers the funds.
"I just don't know the timing yet, but I know that given where we are in the season, we will act accordingly," the HHS spokesman said.
The senators' letter said the need for emergency funds was greater than when Clinton released $180 million in emergency LIHEAP funds last spring.

"In the Northeast and Midwest, the price of home heating oil has jumped at least 22 percent from last year, while natural gas and propane prices in all cold weather states are significantly higher," it said.
